title: SDK oncall smoke rituals and rescue journal
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, portable journal for SDK engineers, oncall responders, and lightweight support rotations. The goal is: 1) give a 2–10 minute ritual to determine whether an SDK incident is a platform issue, client misuse, or network/region degradation; 2) provide tiny reproducible smoke steps to validate a fix; 3) preserve handoff notes so subsequent shifts can pick up without re-running the whole investigation.

Audience
- SDK maintainers and oncall engineers
- Solutions/SEs doing live debugging with customers
- Support folks who need a reproducible minimal reproduction

How to use this document
- Read the top section daily before a shift (2 minutes).
- Use the short checks first, escalate to deeper reproductions only if the short checks fail.
- Add new incident-specific notes at the bottom under a new dated entry.

Daily 90-second ritual (pre-shift)
1) Open the dashboard: Console > SDK > Recent Errors (last 30m). Look for spikes in rate or a cluster of identical error messages.
2) Check the rolling latency p90/p99 (last 5m). If p99 > baseline*3, mark as potential region/capacity event.
3) Quick health curl against hosted endpoint (replace API_KEY placeholder):
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-small-test","input":"ping"}' | jq -r '.status'
   - Expect: "ok" or a short json with tokens. Anything like 429/503 or long tail > 3s moves to escalation.

If you see 429s/503s
- Confirm whether errors map to a single model or all models. Filter errors by model name in the console.
- If only one model: likely model-specific (kernel crash, oom, version mismatch). Add a short reproduction: call the same model with the same input.
- If all models or cross-region: raise priority — possible routing/orchestration/infra issue.

Minimal reproducible checks (order by speed)
A) SDK smoke with minimal payload (5s):
- Node/python quick example (1 line, local token): run the small sample (attached below) from a laptop in the same region as the customer.
- If laptop reproduces -> likely client/usage or credentials; if not, platform.

B) Curl direct to API (2–3s):
- Curl above but add "X-Region" header to test region routing where available.
- Repeat with a different model family: if only quantized model fails, suspect binary/kernel regression.

C) Sample failing prompt/size reproduction (20–60s):
- Use the exact prompt, temperature, max_tokens reported by the customer. Increase a single factor at a time (e.g., double max_tokens) to see if failure scales with memory usage.

Common error fingerprints and immediate actions
- 429 (rate limit): check quotas, burst settings on Dedicated plans, and recent traffic bursts. If a single tokenized endpoint shows spikes, verify client batching/backoff.
- 503 (service unavailable): check runtimes in Console (Serving nodes status). If nodes UNHEALTHY, open incident with infra and set notices in #prod-incidents.
- 400/422 (bad request): copy payload into a local validator (mini script below). Often prompt serialization or invalid function schema.
- Model mismatch / schema errors: confirm model name/version pinned by customer. If mismatch, propose canary rollback to previous model.

Tiny diagnostic scripts (copy-paste)
1) Rapid validator (python)
import requests, os, time
API_KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, json={'model':'redwood-small-test','input':'ping'})
print(resp.status_code, resp.text[:400])

2) Payload size checker (bash)
PAYLOAD='{"model":"redwood-small-test","input":"'$(head -c 4000 /dev/urandom | base64)'"}'
echo ${#PAYLOAD}

Telemetry queries to run (Console/Clickhouse quick snippets)
- error_count by model, by region, last 30m
- latencies (p50/p90/p99) for requests with status != 200
- token cost per request (to detect cost spikes from unintended token inflation)

Handoff checklist (what to leave for next shift)
- Short description of observed symptom (1 line)
- Commands run and results (paste responses)
- Suspected root cause (one sentence)
- Next action (who to call, which eng team, or whether to roll back a model)
- Links to traces/trace ids and the ticket in Linear/Jira

Sample incident vignette (2026-02-06)
- Symptom: sudden p99 latency jumps for SDK v0.8.2 customers in us-west-2, many 503s.
- Quick checks: curl from laptop in us-west-2 returned 200 but slow (1.8s); curl with X-Region: us-east-1 returned 200 in 120ms. Console showed one serving pool reporting GPU OOMs and rapid restarts.
- Action taken: scaled the affected serving pool by +20% capacity, disabled an experimental kernel flag in the deployment rollout, opened PR to pin kernel flag.

Known quick mitigations (non-ideal but fast)
- Temporarily route customers to stable model variant (v0.8.1) with the routing override UI (Console > Routes > Override).
- Apply small token limit to requests from suspect keys to avoid cascading OOMs.

Edge cases and unanswered questions
- How do we handle consistent 400s that appear only with SDK 0.9 but not curl? (Likely serialization differences; need a deterministic diff tool.)
- Should support have the ability to rotate a customer to a different region via Console? (manual today; UX ask filed: SDK-423)

Next steps (short-term)
- Build a 1-click "smoke reproduce" button in the Console that runs the curl validator against the customer key (owner: Jonah Li, ETA: 2026-03-20). See linked PR.
- Add an SDK instrument: capture the raw serialized payload and headers in telemetry for 5xxs only (privacy review required).

Appendix: quick-copy links and snippets
- Minimal python smoke script (same as above)
- Short curl example (same as top)
- Where to paste handoff notes: create Linear ticket, tag #sdk-oncall, paste this doc link and include trace ids.

If you add a dated entry below, please include: date, brief summary, commands run, outcome, and next action.

---
Dated entries (history)
2026-02-06 — see incident vignette above.
2026-02-28 — minor telemetry false positive: an internal test harness emitted malformed function_call metadata; root cause: test harness env var. Mitigation: filter test keys from production telemetry.

Quick TODOs for this doc
- Convert the tiny scripts into a single binary that runs region checks, and returns a structured summary for handoffs (owner: Ethan Park).
- Add a one-liner to rotate a user to stable model variant (Console UX + permission check).
- Validate privacy/PII implications of storing serialized prompts in telemetry (ask: security & privacy).

Notes to self
- Keep this <= 1 page. Oncall docs that read like a novel don't get used.
- When in doubt, favor the curl reproduction — it's the least leaky and fastest to share in Slack.
